questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was two universitys, who offered the program i was looking for. 
Ghent university had a good rumor.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
We had a welcome day, which was somewhat helpful. 
We were assigned tutors, but the welcome day was not required for them, so very few showed up. Overall my tutors did very little to help me during my stay. 
On the first school day we were left on our own to try to find the right place to be and there was very little introduction to the jobs we were expected to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, just have to be careful as there is many scammers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its nice to have some privacy and calm. Youre constantly sorrounded by new people and languages that are not your own at school so a calm base was the right choice for me. I did miss the social opportunities of living around the other exhange students as we were quite spread out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It might be nicer living in student housing, for the extra social oportunities. Other students did complain about it being noisy and dirty though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
My application process was very slow as the university didnt accept my ID card and i had to get additional from home. 
I dont think this reflects the normal procedure though. 
The registration is done via mail and you just have to provide a little information and your ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An email for the responsible coordinater at the university was provided.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was allowed to wish for certain rotations and about half were granted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Reply fast when that ask what rotations you wish for. 
Your ID should match the exact name you are registered at your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I did a mixed program between horses, ruminants and small animals in veterinary medicine. 
The quality of teaching was very varying not just between department but also personel. 
Overall i had expected better.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did clinical rotations for my master program in veterinary medicine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The amount of teachers/vets to students was low. 
The students are expected to do more menial labour with no learning outcome. 
There was a lot of waiting for vets, with nothing else to do. No alternative exercises to use the time was offered. 
You had to constantly remind a lot of teachers and students to speak english or you wouldnt learn anything.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Mixed clinical rotations in horses, ruminants and small animals in veterinary medicine.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I wouldnt recommend any courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt explore any sports, clubs etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ghent city is amazingly beautiful. The city center is great, but there is also a lot of nature spots for great walks/runs. I really enjoyed living in this city. 
Brugge is worth a visit also stunningly beautiful, but touristy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Living in Belgium was easy, felt just like home. Making friends with the locals was more difficult. 
I found that the dutch students were very welcoming and more willing to talk english and include you in conversations. 
The belgian students tended to be more closed of and changed back to talking dutch as soon as they got the chance. 
Overall i found it difficult to be included in social activities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak dutch or french or be okay with not understanding half of what is going on around you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the language barrier was the biggest problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to insist on your inclusion by constantly reminding people to talk english, breaking in to conversations and inviting yourself to things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might want to try to house yourself close to the other exchange students. Its nice having someone who is in the same situation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting less insecure about asking for help and getting more secure in figuring things out myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Never feeling settled and secure. We moved department every week, so every monday was a new chaos of figuring out where everything was and what role i was supposed fill. 
The locals students have spent years at the hospital at this point and dont really understand.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
